assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 was the original, decisive experimental verification of the mechanism of mass generation in the Standard Model and answers a central question about the structure of nature. It is a discovery of the kind the prize statutes name, and it required detector and instrument invention at unprecedented scale. The 2013 prize recognised the theory; the experimental discovery has not been recognised.
assessment.attribution: The credited list is larger than the three-laureate limit. The strongest case rests on those who conceived and led the two experiments and the discovery effort: Jenni (ATLAS), Virdee (CMS) and Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at announcement). Della Negra (CMS) and Evans (LHC machine) have strong claims that cannot all be accommodated, so the configuration is contestable and I would revisit it in discussion.
assessment.maturity: Two independent experiments confirmed the discovery in 2012 and the properties (spin-parity, couplings) have been measured with growing precision through Run 2 and Run 3. Interpretation is stable. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among ATLAS, CMS and the LHC accelerator leadership is unresolved and depends on a view of how collaborative credit should be assigned.
I rely on my own recollection of leadership roles and have not verified them against the record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spherical-aberration correction in the electron microscope removed a limit that had stood since Scherzer's 1936 theorem and brought routine sub-angstrom imaging and atomic-resolution spectroscopy to materials, interfaces and catalysts. It is a tool that opened a door onto atoms that could not previously be resolved, and its consequences run through all of materials physics. I view this from my own field and acknowledge a bias toward it, but the case rests on impact that is unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Rose (theory and corrector design), Haider (realisation of the hexapole corrector in TEM) and Urban (STEM/TEM application and the Jülich programme) form a clean trio and were recognised together by the Wolf Prize. The credit can be disputed: Krivanek and Dellby developed the quadrupole-octupole corrector for STEM independently and are not in the supplied credit, so the allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Aberration-corrected instruments have been in wide use for more than twenty years, with independent replication across many laboratories and thousands of published results. This is mature, and indeed late.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views a microscope technique as physics rather than chemistry or materials science is a procedural question.
Priority of Krivanek and Dellby for the STEM corrector may undermine a three-person configuration limited to the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's 2013 detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos, with later identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy and is an original experimental discovery with a clear instrument at its core. It combines a new detection technique at the South Pole with a result about the high-energy universe.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Karle and Spiering were central to the AMANDA precursor and the detector and analysis. Credit is plausible for these three but the collaboration is large, and Baikal and other pioneers (and the DUMAND tradition) have claims in the history of the technique.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed by multiple analyses and by later independent measurements (e.g. ANTARES and KM3NeT in the broader programme), although source identification remains incomplete.
uncertainties: Individual attribution within a large collaboration is difficult.
Source identification remains partial, so the astrophysical interpretation is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene in 2018 opened moire quantum matter, a platform with tunable correlated and topological physics. The experiment was the original observation and the theory of the magic angle gave the guiding principle. Impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Experiment (Jarillo-Herrero group, with Yuan Cao as lead author, who is not credited) and the Bistritzer-MacDonald theory are distinct contributions. I propose Jarillo-Herrero and MacDonald. Bistritzer's role as co-author of the theory is real but supports a two-person recognition more naturally; the supplied names do not include Cao.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups, with fractional Chern insulators and related states reported since. Superconductivity mechanism is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet settled and timing may be slightly early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the nature of the correlated states are not settled.
Early-career experimental lead is outside the credited list, which complicates the experimental credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser (1994) is an invention in the strict sense: a new principle for emitting light based on engineered intersubband transitions, not set by a bulk bandgap. It is an experimentally demonstrated device with major practical use in mid-infrared spectroscopy and sensing.
assessment.attribution: Capasso led the Bell Labs concept and group, Faist was the first author of the demonstration, and Cho supplied the molecular beam epitaxy growth. Kazarinov and Suris proposed intersubband amplification in 1971 and are not in the credited list, so priority for the idea is a point to examine. The Bell Labs trio is otherwise coherent.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of continuous development, commercial devices and independent replication make this fully mature.
uncertainties: Kazarinov-Suris priority for the underlying concept is not part of the supplied credit.
Whether the committee judges it more engineering than fundamental physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realisation of the Mott insulator transition and later quantum gas microscopy turned ultracold atoms in optical lattices into a controllable simulator of Hubbard-type models, letting one observe correlated matter at the level of single atoms. It is a new way of seeing and testing quantum many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Greiner, Mandel, Hansch and Bloch demonstrated the superfluid-Mott transition in 2002 following the Jaksch-Zoller proposal; Esslinger realised fermionic Mott insulators and related experiments. I keep Zoller out of this configuration because his theory credit is better placed in the quantum computing and simulation entries, and I treat the experimental trio as the observers of the original results. Allocation remains contestable.
assessment.maturity: Many groups worldwide have reproduced and extended the results, and the platform is mature. Concrete quantitative contributions to open problems in condensed matter are still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should include the Jaksch-Zoller theory proposal alongside experiment.
The roles of Hansch, Mandel and others in the original Mott experiment are not captured in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity at 26 K in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx, and rapid rise to 55 K in related compounds, established a second family of high-temperature superconductors beyond the cuprates. It was an original materials discovery that created a new field and broad experimental programme.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the original observation; Zhao's group and Xianhui Chen's group raised Tc to 43 and 55 K within weeks. I would credit Hosono as the discoverer and Zhao for the key Tc advances, though Chen's claim is comparable and the three-way allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: The result has been replicated extensively in hundreds of compounds and the structure-property relations are well characterised. The pairing mechanism remains unresolved, which could make recognition feel somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Allocation between the Hosono, Zhao and Chen groups for the Tc increase is unresolved.
No practical application yet comparable to the discovery's scientific weight.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's 2001 proposal of the magic wavelength for lattice trapping and the later demonstrations by Katori and Ye produced optical clocks with fractional uncertainty below 1e-18, an instrument-driven advance in measurement that makes new tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and time redefinition possible.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the original proposal and first demonstration; Ye developed the strontium clock to the highest accuracy and combined it with the frequency comb. A two-person configuration is clear, although Hall and Hansch were already recognised for the comb and other clock groups (NIST ion clocks) hold related credit.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks agree at the 1e-18 level and the SI second redefinition is under discussion. Mature, though the large-scale impact of redefinition is still pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes (frequency combs, ion control) may reduce appetite.
Value to humanity is mainly metrological and still prospective.
